title: SDLC commit signoff & audit evidence procedure
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary
=======
This document defines the standardized commit signoff process, mandatory audit evidence artifacts, and the automated evidence-collection pipeline required for any code or configuration change that affects model-serving, authentication/authorization, data residency, or production runtime behavior. It formalizes what evidence is produced, where it is stored, and how long it must be retained to satisfy internal controls and external audit requests.

Scope
-----
Applies to:
- All repositories and IaC affecting Redwood inference runtime, ingress/egress controls, and deployment manifests.
- All changes that modify RBAC policies, audit-logging configuration, data residency routing, or release gates in the SDLC.
- Private / Dedicated / Hosted deployment manifests that change residency or key management settings.

Definitions
-----------
- Commit signoff: explicit approval metadata attached to a git commit or merge (signed tag, commit signature, or merge approved in the approved pipeline).
- Evidence artifact: reproducible file(s) that demonstrate who approved, what tests ran, and the resulting binary or manifest deployed. Typical artifacts: signed tags, signed SBOM, pipeline runlog, policy approval record, generated evidence-manifest.json.
- Evidence repository: immutable storage (S3 + object lock or audit bucket) where packaged evidence is stored for retention and retrieval.

High-level principles
---------------------
1. Single source of truth: every production-affecting change must reference an evidence-manifest stored alongside the build artifact and the deployment descriptor.
2. Immutable provenance: commits must be GPG-signed or CI-signed; release artifacts must be tagged with an auditable signature.
3. Minimum evidence: keep the evidence set compact and queryable for 7 years for enterprise customers and 3 years for standard hosted usage unless longer retention is required by contract.
4. Automated capture: evidence must be collected automatically by CI/CD and archived without manual upload steps to avoid human error.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Author: the engineer who authored the change; creates the initial evidence bundle.
- Approver: a user with the RBAC role "sdlc-approver" or equivalent; responsible for review and attestation.
- CI Owner: responsible for ensuring pipeline artifacts contain required signatures and metrics.
- Evidence Custodian (Security): curates the evidence retention policy, verifies packaging integrity, runs periodic spot checks.

Commit signoff checklist (must be satisfied before merge to protected branches)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Commit or merge request must include a short rationale and listing of impacted services and residency changes.
2. Automated test matrix must pass: unit, integration, model-serving smoke, data-residency route test.
3. Security checks must pass: static analysis, dependency-scan, license-scan.
4. RBAC impact assessment: either "no change" or a link to the change request in the entitlement system.
5. Evidence-manifest generated and uploaded by pipeline; manifest must include artifact checksums and signatures.
6. Merge must be approved by at least one sdlc-approver; where the change touches customer data residency or cryptographic keys, two approvers are required.

Evidence manifest schema (textual example)
------------------------------------------
An example evidence-manifest.json (CI will generate):

{
  "version": "1.0",
  "commit": "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
  "git_signature": "GPG:0x9F12AB34",
  "pipeline_run_id": "ci-2028-11-15-9834",
  "artifacts": ["service-image:v1.2.3"],
  "sbom": "s3://evidence-bucket/sbom/a1b2c3.json.gpg",
  "approvals": [ {"approver": "s.chen@redwood.ai", "role": "sdlc-approver", "timestamp": "2028-11-15T14:22:00Z" } ],
  "tests_run": ["unit","integration","residency-route-check"],
  "retention_policy": "enterprise-7y"
}

Where evidence is stored
-----------------------
- Short-term: pipeline artifacts kept in the CI artifact store for 90 days (for debugging).
- Long-term (compliance): evidence package (evidence-manifest.json + signed artifacts + logs) uploaded to evidence-bucket with object-lock enabled and tagged with customer and contract ids where applicable.
- Access control: read access only to group "compliance-read" and write access restricted to the CI service principal and Security evidence curator.

Automated collection and verification pipeline
---------------------------------------------
1. Developer pushes branch; CI runs tests and checks.
2. CI generates evidence-manifest.json including artifact checksums and signs it with the CI signing key (HSM-backed recommended).
3. If checks pass, the pipeline calls the entitlement system API to fetch RBAC change records and attaches them to the manifest.
4. Evidence package is encrypted with a KMS key and uploaded to the evidence-bucket. CI inserts the final record into the audit-log topic.
5. A verification job runs daily to validate object-lock flags, signature validity, and manifest-artifact checksum matching for a random sample.

Runbook: responding to an evidence request (auditor or customer)
----------------------------------------------------------------
1. Receipt: Security receives request via compliance intake (jira COMP-REQ-####).
2. Scoping: identify the time window and affected services.
3. Search: query evidence index by commit id, pipeline run id, or customer id.
4. Assemble package: pull evidence-manifest and all referenced artifacts into a temporary staging bucket.
5. Verify signatures and checksums locally.
6. Produce export: sign an export manifest and deliver using secure share link (timebound) or legal-approved transfer mechanism.
7. Log delivery and update request ticket with TTL and recipient identity.

SLOs and operational metrics
---------------------------
- Evidence retrieval SLA: 24 business hours for requests that specify commit id; 3 business days for open-ended historical searches.
- Packaging success rate: 99% of pipeline runs must produce a valid evidence-manifest.
- Signature verification: 100% of long-term artifacts must be verifiable by the evidence custodian within 30 days of creation.

Exception handling and risk controls
-----------------------------------
- If the CI pipeline cannot produce an evidence-manifest (e.g., external outage), teams must not merge to protected branch and must open an exception request.
- Temporary exceptions follow the Authorization Exception workflow: create a control-exception record, attach compensating controls (e.g., extended logging, third-party witness), and include an evidence-retention override with explicit expiry.
- Security will approve short-lived exceptions only under emergency criteria; longer exceptions routed to GRC and legal.

Table: minimal evidence checklist by change type
------------------------------------------------
Change type | Minimum artifacts | Extra controls required
------------|-------------------|------------------------
RBAC policy change | evidence-manifest, policy-diff, approver list | post-deploy entitlement scan
Data-residency routing | manifest, integration test logs, KMS policy change | residency proof (e.g., trace of regional endpoints)
Release that touches model weights | sbom, artifact-sig, license-scan | model-weights-hash + provenance doc
Hotfix to production | evidence-manifest, CI-runlog, hotfix-approver | retrospective postmortem within 3 days

(Represented above in ascii table format; the CI will produce a machine-readable CSV in the evidence package.)

Developer and CI examples
-------------------------
- GPG sign commit: git commit -S -m "update residency routes for eu region"
- Tagging a release: git tag -s v1.2.3 -m "release for residency fix" && git push origin v1.2.3
- CI command to export evidence: 
  ./ci/export-evidence --run-id $CI_RUN_ID --destination s3://evidence-bucket/staging/$CI_RUN_ID --kms-key arn:aws:kms:...

Audit considerations (mapping to frameworks)
------------------------------------------
- SOC2: evidence manifest fulfills CC8.1/CC8.2 style requirements by demonstrating change logging and approval.
- ISO27001: packaged evidence supports control A.12 and A.9 change control attestations.
- Contractual: when a customer contract demands longer retention, the evidence-manifest must include customer_retention_tag and route packaging to the contractual-compliance tier.

Periodic review and maintenance
-------------------------------
- Quarterly: Security runs a random sample verification across 3% of all long-term evidence packages.
- Annual: update retention durations and KMS rotation schedule; confirm alignment with legal obligations.
- On-call: the Evidence Custodian rotation handles immediate access requests outside normal SLAs.

Appendix A: common failure modes and mitigations
-----------------------------------------------
- Missing signature on manifest: pipeline rejects merge; mitigation: re-run signing step and revalidate artifact checksums.
- Object-lock not applied: automated remediation job re-applies lock and notifies Security; if remediation fails, open incident SEC-EVID-LOCK-01.
- Retention mismatch for a customer: Evidence Custodian creates an override and notifies legal; update tags and re-archive copy to the customer-specific vault.

Appendix B: contact and escalation matrix
----------------------------------------
- Evidence Custodian (Primary): security-evidence@redwood.ai
- CI Owner (Secondary): infra-ci@redwood.ai
- Security Director (Escalation): a.patel@redwood.ai

Related artifacts and automation repos
-------------------------------------
- ci/export-evidence (internal repo)
- compliance-inventory (index service)
- evidence-bucket lifecycle policies (S3 path: /policies/sdlc-evidence-lifecycle.yaml)
